articles.title: Amit Mishra Joins Star-Studded Delhi Capitals Coaching Staff For IPL 2027: Check Full List
articles.description: Delhi Capitals Coaching Staff For IPL 2027: Former India leg-spinner Amit Mishra has joined Delhi Capitals as their spin-bowling coach ahead of IPL 2027, adding another experienced name to the franchise's revamped coaching setup. Mishra joins a group led by former India captain Sourav Ganguly, with Yuvraj Singh and former Sri Lanka pacer Chaminda Vaas also taking up coaching roles. The appointment marks Mishra's return to the Delhi franchise, where his IPL journey began. The 43-year-old retired from all forms of cricket in September 2025 and will now begin his coaching career in the league with the same franchise he represented as a player. Mishra finished his IPL career with 174 wickets and remains the only bowler to have taken three hat-tricks in the tournament's history. His experience in the competition will be an addition to Delhi Capitals' spin-bowling department as the team prepares for the 2027 season. Delhi Capitals Coaching Staff For IPL 2027: Full List Head Coach: Sourav Ganguly Assistant Coach: Yuvraj Singh Fast-Bowling Coach: Chaminda Vaas Spin-Bowling Coach: Amit Mishra Sourav Ganguly To Lead Delhi Capitals' New Coaching Setup Ganguly will take charge as Delhi Capitals' head coach after previously being associated with the franchise in different roles. The former India captain has also coached Pretoria Capitals in South Africa's SA20 league and worked with Delhi Capitals in the Women's Premier League. Yuvraj, meanwhile, will work as assistant and batting coach. The former India all-rounder is beginning his formal coaching career after years of mentoring young Indian players. His appointment reunites him with Ganguly, under whom he played for India. Vaas brings international playing and coaching experience to the pace-bowling department. The former Sri Lanka left-arm fast bowler has worked with Sri Lanka's teams and also held coaching and consultancy roles involving New Zealand and Ireland. Mishra's appointment completes the four-person coaching group outlined above. Delhi Capitals will hope the experience of the former India internationals helps the team prepare for the 2027 campaign as they continue their pursuit of a maiden IPL title.

articles.title: 'Pathetic': David Warner Makes Blunt Remark Over Poor Crowd At South Africa vs Australia Test
articles.description: David Warner has voiced his frustration over the lack of spectators at the ongoing Test series between South Africa and Australia, questioning whether the longest format can truly be considered cricket’s premier contest when stadiums remain largely empty. The former Aussie opener took to his official X account to highlight the disappointing attendance and atmosphere. The ongoing series has therefore sparked debate beyond the results, with crowd attendance emerging as a concern for the future appeal of Test cricket. Warner Questions Test Cricket’s Popularity After Poor Turnout Warner did not hold back in his assessment of the scenes in South Africa, pointing to the contrast between the format’s reputation and the limited number of fans watching from the stands. "We keep hearing how important Test cricket is, but where are the fans in South Africa? Empty stands, no atmosphere, and we’re supposed to believe the format is thriving? You can’t keep calling Test cricket the pinnacle of the game if no one turns up to watch it. Harsh reality, but someone has to say it. Pathetic," The former opener’s post focused on the visible gaps in the crowd and the subdued atmosphere at the venues. Australia’s Durban Victory Fails To Fill The Stands The attendance issue was evident during the opening Test in Durban, where Australia secured a 214-run victory over South Africa at Kingsmead. Despite the significance of the international contest, substantial portions of the stadium were left unoccupied. The sparse turnout has become a talking point because the series features two leading cricket nations. The lack of spectators is particularly notable for South Africa, who entered the contest as reigning ICC World Test Champions. While the quality of competition remains high, Warner’s criticism highlights the importance of building stronger connections between Test cricket and its audience. Consistent support at the ground contributes not only to ticket revenue but also to the atmosphere that makes international sport compelling.

Swati, who is making her Games debut, also assured India of at least a silver medal after beating South Korea's Eunhee Lee 6-2 in the women's W1 semifinal. She will face China's Mengkan in the final. W1 classification is for athletes with significant impairment in functional strength, range of motion, or limb loss across all four limbs.
